walkthrough:
**Set up the hypotheses (first B1)**

Before the update the mean rate was 2.1 faults per week. We tested over 20 weeks, so we scale the rate to 20 weeks:

$$2.1 \times 20 = 42 \text{ faults in 20 weeks}$$

Let $\lambda$ be the population mean number of faults in 20 weeks. The management want to know if the rate has **changed**, which could mean up or down, so the alternative is two-sided:

$$\text{H}_0:\ \lambda = 42 \qquad \text{H}_1:\ \lambda \neq 42$$

(Writing $\text{H}_0$ as 'the population mean weekly rate is 2.1' also earns the credit. Check that the symbols are defined.)

**Why we use a normal approximation (B1 ft)**

If $\text{H}_0$ is true, the number of faults in 20 weeks follows a Poisson distribution, $X \sim \text{Po}(42)$. The question tells us to use an approximation. When $\lambda$ is large (over about 10) a Poisson distribution is close to a normal distribution with the same mean and variance. For a Poisson, the mean and variance are both $\lambda$:

$$X \sim \text{Po}(42) \approx \text{N}(42,\ 42)$$

Quick check: the variance is 42, so the standard deviation is $\sqrt{42} = 6.4807$.

**Continuity correction (M1)**

Faults are whole numbers (discrete) but the normal is continuous. So each whole number $54$ is treated as the range from $53.5$ to $54.5$.

We saw 54 faults, which is **more** than the 42 expected under $\text{H}_0$. So we look at the upper tail: the probability of getting 54 **or more**.

$$\text{P}(X \geqslant 54) \to \text{P}(X > 53.5)$$

We use $53.5$ because it is the lower edge of 54 and includes it. Now standardise:

$$z = \frac{53.5 - 42}{\sqrt{42}}$$

This line earns the M1.

**Calculate $z$ (A1)**

$$53.5 - 42 = 11.5$$

$$\frac{11.5}{6.4807} = 1.774$$

So $z = 1.774$ (the scheme accepts $1.77$ too, and accepts the answer without the continuity correction). If you compare areas instead: $\text{P}(Z > 1.774) = 1 - \Phi(1.774) = 0.038$.

**Compare with the critical value (M1)**

This is a two-tailed test at the 5% level. So 2.5% is in each tail, and the critical value is $1.96$. We reject $\text{H}_0$ only if $z$ is above $1.96$ (or below $-1.96$).

$$1.774 < 1.96$$

Area method: $0.038 > 0.025$ (half of 5%), which gives the same result.

**Conclusion in context (A1 ft)**

Our $z$ is not in the rejection region. So we do **not** reject $\text{H}_0$. There is not enough evidence at the 5% level to say the rate has changed.

Use wording such as 'no evidence', not 'the rate has not changed'. A test cannot prove $\text{H}_0$ is true. Also, do not contradict yourself: if you wrote 'accept $\text{H}_0$', you cannot also say 'the rate has changed'.

**Final answer**

$z = 1.774 < 1.96$ (or $0.038 > 0.025$), so $\text{H}_0$ is not rejected. There is no evidence, at the 5% significance level, that the mean rate of computer faults has changed.
